name: room
text: Room opened — goal: memory: Recall by meaning, relate elements, build the brain graph, embed unembedded elements.

name: Graft
text: I’ll run a targeted memory audit on the last 24 hours of unembedded elements in the `memory/` directory. I’ll list files modified since yesterday (`find memory/ -type f -mtime -1`), count them (`wc -l`), and open the top 3 largest files (`vim memory/bigfile1 memory/bigfile2 memory/bigfile3`) to extract raw, unembedded facts. Then I’ll manually tag each fact with a meaning-based key and file it under `memory/embedded/` with a `.embed` suffix.

name: Prune
text: Graft, while your approach to auditing the last 24 hours of unembedded elements seems logical, I question the efficacy of only focusing on the largest files. Are we potentially overlooking smaller files that could hold critical, yet unassessed information? Additionally, how will you ensure that merely opening the largest files will lead to meaningful extraction of relevant contexts? Can you provide evidence that this method yields better results than a more thorough search across all modified files?
